status: Working result. Scoped independent local review completed; formal review pending.

conventions.wall: Fixed-intake passive local wall, normal displacement b f cos(theta) in both halves, f=sin²(pi w/H). Mass per angular slice is already integrated over its area. One draining carrier. The field forces and radiation are retained from the archived frequency-dependent response.
conventions.front: Trial reversible kinetic coefficient I_B for a thin, translated equilibrium order front in a fixed unperturbed material reference. Isotropic kappa_B, negligible curvature corrections on thickness scale and negligible wall-relative advection/loading beyond the archived kernels. Front saturates the side tension and archived radial calibration. The real-scalar inertia is newly posited. Width and tension alone do not set I_B. No independent calibration of c_order on this preparation.
conventions.bound: Given fixed total positive wall mass on a constant-area cylinder and target t=3 M_fold/M_radial, let g=sin^4(pi u). A=integral of (g−t)_+. For depth contrast C, integral h(g−t)/min(h) <= 3/8−t+(C−1)A. Equality puts the maximal density wherever g>t and the minimum elsewhere. Speed ratio interpretation additionally requires constant tension and the front law. Tested resolved high-mass branch only.
conventions.spectrum: Same stiffness 0.424660352295, carrier and wave kernels, equal-area 1:3-width selective readout, common shift and zero additional dephasing. Assumes low-frequency wall inertia persists across spectral drive frequencies. The fixed-end bend supplies no calibration of free-body inertia.

review.verdict: Scoped clear for the conditional thin-front mass projection and the sharp minimum depth contrast at the archived fine spectral fold.
review.scope: Independent source audit, numerical integration with a separate implementation, and three depth-grid linear programs. Peak count checked against previously archived uniform spectrum. The primary Python calculation reevaluated both meshes. Mathematica independently integrated the thin-front norm, laboratory and conjugate momenta and checked the primitive used in the bound.
review.qualification: A convected order variable moves relative to the local material velocity. The reversible trial law is new and needs an independent speed measurement. Positive profiles with smooth depth variation approach the optimum. A large contrast is only necessary unless its placement is known.
